transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main thing is at work. I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing claims. It’s been getting in the way enough that I thought I should come talk to someone.
When you get up from your workstation, do you feel restless inside?
I don’t know if I’d call it restless inside exactly. It’s more that I keep getting up from my workstation during the day, even when I know I’m supposed to stay there and finish reviewing the claims.
Before you get up from your workstation, do you have a thought that you can’t ignore and feel you have to act on?

I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a specific thought like that. It’s more like I just realize I’m up already, or I decide to step away for a second, but I don’t know that it feels like something I can’t ignore.
Did you have problems sitting still or staying focused like this when you were a child?

Yeah, looking back, it wasn’t totally new. In elementary school, I remember teachers writing things like I was bright, but I’d lose worksheets, miss instructions, and need reminders to finish my classwork.
At work, do you often have trouble staying focused on the claims you’re reviewing?

Yes, pretty often. If people near me start talking about another claim, or I suddenly remember some random errand I need to do, my attention just kind of slides off what I’m reading. Then I realize I didn’t take it in, and I have to reread the same section a few times.
Do you have similar trouble staying focused in other parts of your life outside of work?

Yeah, I think so. It’s similar outside of work too—if I’m trying to read something or focus on something at home and I hear people talking nearby, or I suddenly remember some random errand, I just lose the thread. Then I have to go back and reread what I was looking at because I didn’t really take it in.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?
Not really, no. I mean, I have frustrating days, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day over the last couple weeks.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to deal with?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry about normal stuff when something’s actually going on, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying a lot when there isn’t a problem.

final_diagnosis.reason: Presentation is most consistent with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, unspecified: the patient reports persistent inattention symptoms across work and home settings, a history of similar symptoms in childhood, and associated occupational impairment. There is also behavioral hyperactivity/fidgetiness reflected by repeatedly leaving the workstation. Depression and generalized anxiety were not supported, and the behavior did not appear driven by obsessions or compulsions.
